papers.title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.authors: Liu Z, Liu Y, Li S, Zhang X, Qiang R, Jin F et al.
papers.abstract:
Since surgery can only remove lesions of a larger size visible to the naked eye, the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery is high. In recent years, numerous scholars have found that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) treatment is effective in reducing the recurrence rate of postoperative fibroids, as well as improving the clinical treatment rate, regulating serum hormone levels, reducing plasma viscosity, and promoting the restoration of uterine volume following surgery. Several randomized controlled trials have been undertaken on the prevention and treatment of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids using patented Chinese medicines and self-proposed formulations, such as Guizhi Fuling Pill, Xiaozheng decoction, Xiangleng pill, Zhengjia decoction, Xiaoliu decoction, Guizhi Jiliu pill, Huoxue Huayu formula, Huoxue Xiaozheng decoction, Shugan Sanjie decoction, Gongliuxiao capsule, Hongjin Xiaojie concentrated pill, and Jiawei Guizhi Fuling decoction. However, no study has systematically evaluated Chinese herbal medicine (CHM) in reducing the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after surgery.
This study aimed to conduct a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials of CHM for the prevention of postoperative recurrence of uterine fibroids, evaluating its efficacy and safety.
A comprehensive search was conducted on PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, China National Knowledge Infrastructure (CNKI), VIP Information Database (VIP), WanFang Database, and China Biomedical Database (CBM) to identify randomized controlled clinical studies conducted up to March 2025 that examined the efficacy of CHM in treating patients with postoperative uterine fibroids. Two institutes were independently under-selected, and data were extracted and quality assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2.0 tool. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager software 5.4, and forest plots were generated. The quality of evidence was assessed using GRADEpro 3.2.2. This study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251000288).
16 trials were included in this study, and the postoperative recurrence rate after treatment was mainly analyzed. CHM treatment reduces postoperative recurrence rates in patients with uterine fibroids compared to the blank (6 trials, n = 588; OR (odds ratio) = 0.22; 95 % CI (95 % confidence intervals) = 0.14-0.34; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001), conventional western medicine (CWM) (1 trial, n = 80; OR = 0.30; 95 % CI = 0.09-0.93, p = 0.04), and combined CHM with CWM (9 trials, n = 959; OR = 0.29; 95 % CI = 0.19-0.46; I2 = 0 %, p < 0.00001). In addition, CHM is also effective in improving clinical efficiency, restoring serum sex hormone levels, lowering plasma viscosity, and reducing uterine volume. CHM is generally considered safe, with a low incidence of adverse reactions.
CHM is effective in avoiding recurrence of uterine fibroids after surgery, excelling in terms of overall effectiveness, restoring female hormone levels, improving hemorheological indices, and promoting uterine recovery and safety. However, these findings are preliminary and still need to be validated by higher-quality studies.

papers.title: Network pharmacology-based identification and experimental validation of active compounds from Qingda Granules against Ang II-induced hypertension.
papers.authors: Zhang L, Ali F, Wu M, Guo Z, Lin G, Zhang X et al.
papers.abstract:
Hypertension is a significant global health issue that raises the risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). Qingda Granule (QDG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used to treat hypertension, but its active compounds and mechanisms of action remain poorly understood.
Network pharmacology identified potential active compounds and KEGG pathways. Four compounds-gastrodin, rhynchophylline, baicalin, and liensinine were selected. Hypertension was induced in mice via Angiotensin II (Ang II) infusion. QDG (1145 mg/kg/day) or each compound (10 mg/kg/day) was administered orally once daily. Outcomes measured included systolic blood pressure (SBP), diastolic blood pressure (DBP), mean arterial pressure (MAP), pulse wave velocity (PWV), and abdominal aortic wall thickness. Histological examination and immunohistochemistry for expression of total myosin light chain (MLC) and phosphorylation of myosin light chain (p-MLC) were performed in exploratory subgroups of three mice per group.
Network pharmacology analysis identified 482 predicted targets overlapping with hypertension-related targets. The compound-target network was constructed and analyzed, and hub nodes were identified using multiple parameters, such as betweenness centrality and degree. These four selected compounds-gastrodin, rhynchophylline, baicalin, and liensinine-ranked among the top 50 nodes in the compound-target network. Consequently, these four compounds were selected for further validation. KEGG enrichment analysis identified vascular smooth muscle contraction as an enriched candidate pathway (18 targets). In vivo, QDG and all four compounds treatment significantly lowered blood pressure, lowered PWV, and reduced abdominal aortic wall thickness. Exploratory subgroup analyses showed attenuated aortic histopathological changes and reduced p-MLC immunoreactivity, with no significant difference in total MLC immunoreactivity in abdominal aortic tissues of Ang II-infused mice.
QDG and its four individually administered compounds attenuated blood pressure elevation and were associated with lower PWV and reduced abdominal aortic wall thickening in Ang II-infused mice, as well as reduced p-MLC immunoreactivity. These findings suggest that the QDG and its four compounds contribute to antihypertensive effects.

papers.title: Response surface optimisation of Xiaoyao San polyphenols and anti-inflammatory activity in colonic epithelial cells.
papers.authors: Huang YX, Que ZQ, Cheng Y, Zheng FP, Chen XQ
papers.abstract: Xiaoyao San is a traditional Chinese medicine formula, but its polyphenol extraction and intestinal epithelial activity remain insufficiently defined. We optimised ethanol-reflux extraction by response surface methodology and evaluated the polyphenol-rich fraction in NCM460 cells. The validated optimum was 57% ethanol, a 7.6 mL/g liquid-solid ratio, and 94 min, yielding 7.44 ± 0.15 mg gallic acid equivalents per gram. Xiaoyao San increased cell viability and proliferation, reduced apoptosis and nitrite accumulation, and decreased TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6 concentrations. Molecular docking predicted favourable interactions between selected polyphenols and NLRP3, while immunoblotting showed lower NLRP3, caspase-1, and ASC abundance after treatment. The low concentration frequently produced equal or greater effects than the high concentration. These findings connect extraction optimisation with epithelial protection and support chemical standardisation, direct target-engagement studies.

papers.title: Effect of YiFei SanJie Formula on persistent pure ground-glass nodules: a multicenter prospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Li J, Zhou M, Han W, Jiao L, Liu Y, Guo W et al.
papers.abstract: Persistent pure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) are one of the main imaging manifestations of early-stage lung cancer. However, there is a lack of effective treatment methods except surgical resection. To assess the effectiveness of YiFei SanJie Formula (YFSJF) on pGGNs, we conducted a multicenter prospective cohort study. This study was conducted in four centers in China. The clinical efficacy difference between the YFSJF group and non-YFSJF treatment was compared during the 2-year follow-up. The primary outcome was growth rate. The secondary outcomes included regression rate, volume of pGGN, maximum diameter of pGGN in axial plane, and mean CT attenuation of pGGN in axial plane. From January 2021 to December 2022, 63 patients dropped out. Ultimately, 717 patients (91.9%) were included in the final analysis. After 2-year follow-up, pGGN growth was observed in 27 patients (7.2%) in the YFSJF group, compared to 48 patients (14%) in the non-YFSJF (OR, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.29-0.79; P = 0.004). pGGN regression was observed in 27 patients (7.2%) in the YFSJF group, compared to 13 patients (3.8%) in the non-YFSJF group (OR, 2.31; 95% CI, 1.15-4.65; P = 0.019). In the multivariable analysis, the YFSJF group had a significant effect on the volume change of pGGNs compared with the non-YFSJF group (P < 0.001). However, maximum diameter and mean CT attenuation did not significantly differ between the two groups (P > 0.05). During the 2-year follow-up period, YFSJF may have a certain effect on pGGNs, which can delay the growth of pGGNs and improve the regression.

papers.title: Isoformononetin alleviates depression through regulating neuroinflammation and mitochondrial homeostasis by targeting PDE4D.
papers.journal: Journal of neuroimmune pharmacology : the official journal of the Society on NeuroImmune Pharmacology
papers.authors: Chu H, Zheng Y, Zheng S, Zhang Y, Kong L, Zhang H
papers.abstract: Depression is a common neuropsychiatric illness characterized by reduced energy, decreased interest or pleasure in activities and persistent feelings of sadness, causing severe burden on both patients and society as its continuously rising incidence, underscoring an urgent need for developing novel antidepressants. Danggui Buxue Decoction (DBD) is a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula traditionally indicated for deficiency patterns. However, whether DBD can alleviate depression, the bioactive constituents and molecular basis remain unexplored. Here, we evaluated the antidepression activities of DBD and identified isoformononetin (IFM) as the key bioactive constituent in chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced mouse model. IFM ameliorated depressive‑like behaviors and hippocampal tissue damages induced by CUMS, while increased serum levels of 5-hydroxytryptamine (5-HT). Mechanistically, IFM bound to phosphodiesterase 4D (PDE4D) protein and promoted its ubiquitination-dependent degradation, thereby activating the cAMP-CREB-BDNF signaling axis and regulating mitochondrial homeostasis. Moreover, IFM ameliorated neuroinflammation via reducing NOD-like receptor thermal protein domain associated protein 3 (NLRP3) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unpublished mechanism by which the phytochemical IFM exerts neuroprotective and anti‑inflammatory effects, positioning IFM as a potential antidepressant agent and laying the groundwork for the development of innovative clinical treatment approaches.

papers.title: Astragaloside IV-Loaded PRP-Exosomes Promote Angiogenic Functions in HUVECs: Association with Jagged-1/Notch Pathway Activation.
papers.journal: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology
papers.authors: Wu J, Chen B, Fang R, Zhu Z, Yang X, Suo Y
papers.abstract:
Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) exhibits prominent pro-angiogenic activity. Platelet-rich plasma-derived exosomes (PRP-Exos) serve as natural nanocarriers with intrinsic tissue-repairing activity. This study aimed to construct AS-IV-loaded PRP-Exos (AS-IV/PRP-Exos) and investigate their combined regulatory effects on the functions of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs).
PRP-Exos were extracted by ultracentrifugation and characterized by western blot, transmission electron microscopy, and nanoparticle tracking analysis. AS-IV was loaded into PRP-Exos via sonication, and the encapsulation efficiency was determined by high-performance liquid chromatography. The cellular uptake of PKH67-labeled exosomes by HUVECs was observed via fluorescence microscopy. A high-glucose-induced HUVEC injury model was established, and cells were treated with AS-IV, PRP-Exos, or AS-IV/PRP-Exos to assess cell viability, migration, and tube formation. The expression of angiogenesis-related and Notch pathway molecules was detected by RT-qPCR and Western blot. Finally, exogenous Jagged-1 was introduced as an intervention to observe its effects.
The extracted PRP-Exos exhibited typical exosomal morphology, with an AS-IV encapsulation efficiency of 49.82%, and were effectively internalized by HUVECs. Compared with AS-IV or PRP-Exos monotherapy, AS-IV/PRP-Exos significantly enhanced HUVEC viability, migration, and tube formation. Mechanistically, AS-IV/PRP-Exos downregulated the expression of VEGF and DLL4, while upregulating the expression of CD31, E-cadherin, and Jagged-1. Additionally, AS-IV/PRP-Exos elevated cleaved Notch1, Hes1, and Hey1 expression. Importantly, exogenous Jagged-1 reversed these effects and attenuated the functional improvements induced by AS-IV/PRP-Exos.
This study provides experimental evidence for the combined application of active ingredients from traditional Chinese medicine and exosome-based delivery system.

papers.title: Protective Effects of the Standardized Extract of Amburana cearensis in an Experimental Model of Severe Asthma: Suppression of Airway Inflammation and Modulation of Neutrophil Function.
papers.journal: Advances in pharmacological and pharmaceutical sciences
papers.authors: Amaral HHS, Rocha TM, Araújo EVO, de Araújo AB, Bezerra AME, Evangelista JSAM et al.
papers.abstract: Amburana cearensis A.C. Smith (Fabaceae) is traditionally used in Brazilian medicine for the treatment of asthma; however, its effects in experimental models of asthma exacerbation remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the effects of a standardized dried extract of A. cearensis (DEAC) and its chemical constituents-coumarin (CM) and vanillic acid (VA)-on airway inflammation in a murine model of ovalbumin (OVA) + lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced asthma exacerbation and on human neutrophil activation. DEAC was characterized by high-performance liquid chromatography with photodiode array detection (HPLC-PDA) (markers: CM, VA, and amburoside). BALB/c mice were sensitized and challenged with OVA + LPS and treated with DEAC (100 mg/kg) and CM. On Day 26, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) and lungs were analyzed for total and differential leukocytes, cytokines interleukin-4 (IL-4) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and histopathological changes. The effects of DEAC, CM, and VA on phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced human neutrophil activation were assessed through myeloperoxidase release and reactive oxygen species (ROS) production by chemiluminescence. OVA + LPS challenge induced severe airway inflammation, characterized by increased leukocyte recruitment, predominance of neutrophils, elevated IL-4 and TNF-α levels, and mucus hypersecretion. DEAC markedly reduced total leukocyte accumulation, restored the mononuclear cell proportion, and decreased neutrophil and eosinophil infiltration, with effects comparable to dexamethasone. CM reduced neutrophil accumulation without affecting total leukocytes. Lung histology confirmed decreased inflammation and mucus production. DEAC also lowered IL-4 and TNF-α levels. DEAC, CM, and VA inhibited neutrophil degranulation and ROS generation without affecting cell viability. These findings demonstrate the anti-inflammatory potential of A. cearensis and support its traditional use as an adjuvant therapy for asthma within Brazilian public phytotherapy programs.

papers.title: Fabrication of carbon dots derived from Alangium salviifolium for the sequential sensing Ag+ and S2- and further monitoring of H2S in spoiled food.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Qi X, Yang H, Xu D, Cui T, Dai Q, Chen G et al.
papers.abstract: Given the significant threat posed by heavy metals to ecological system and human health, the development of precise, portable, and on-site analytical technologies is urgently required. Herein, multifunctional carbon dots (A-CDs) derived from the traditional chinese medicine (TCM) were synthesized and exhibited optimal emission at 604 nm excited at 495 nm, with quantum yield (QY) of 18.25%. The A-CDs achieved the cascade determination of Ag+ and S2- via a subsequent "on-off-on" process with LODs of 63.7 nM and 0.98 μM, respectively. Notably, A-CDs portable platform was constructed and enabled on-site quantitative analysis with LODs of 0.83 μM and 1.19 μM, respectively. Leveraging this unique sensing performance, the A-CDs test strips were developed for visual screening of H2S during food spoilage at varying storage temperatures, allowing qualitative food freshness discrimination via naked-eye observation. The precise quantitative detection in real water and foodstuff was applied, and further verified by ICP-MS, confirmed the excellent accuracy and environmental tolerance. This work presented an intelligent strategy for designing cost-effective, high-performance multivariate probes, holding significant promise for advancing food safety and environmental monitoring.

papers.title: A dual-signal sensor for highly selective and reliable detection of rutin based on molecularly imprinted Prussian blue analogue.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Xu J, Wang H, Bai H, Li J, Li H, Ma D
papers.abstract: The reliable and accurate quantification of rutin is essential for pharmaceutical quality control, pharmacokinetic investigations, and clinical applications, owing to its broad pharmacological activities. In this study, we address this need by developing a novel dual-mode sensing platform based on a molecularly imprinted polymer-coated bimetallic Prussian blue analogue (Mn/FePBA@MIP). The Mn/FePBA@MIP analogue not only exhibits high peroxidase-like catalytic activity via its synergistic bimetallic sites but also possesses target-specific recognition capability through its surface-imprinted cavities. Upon specific rebinding of rutin, the imprinted polymer layer blocks substrate access to the catalytic sites via a gatekeeper effect, thereby quenching both the colorimetric and fluorescent signals. Under optimized conditions, the developed sensor achieves wide linear detection ranges of 6-1536 μg mL-1 for the colorimetric mode and 6-3072 μg mL-1 for the fluorescent mode, with corresponding detection limits of 3.98 μg mL-1 and 1.32 μg mL-1, respectively. For on-site applications, the sensor was integrated with a smartphone-based readout system for quantitative analysis via RGB value extraction, and successfully applied to determine rutin in traditional Chinese medicine samples with satisfactory recoveries. This work thus provides a reliable and portable dual-signal strategy for routine quality assurance of rutin-related herbal products.

papers.title: Research on the composition of total flavonoid aglycones in Clematis aethusifolia Turcz. and its effects on HaCaT cells and melanin.
papers.authors: Longwei F, La Y, Zhuoma D, Parbeen S, Hebing X, Jie L et al.
papers.abstract: Solar dermatitis is driven by UV-induced oxidative stress and pigmentation disorders. Clematis aethusifolia Turcz., a traditional Chinese medicine used empirically for solar dermatitis and melasma, lacks mechanistic understanding. This study characterised its flavonoid aglycones and evaluated their photoprotective and anti-melanogenic effects. High‑performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) identified quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin and apigenin as major aglycones. The flavonoids (≤80 μg/mL) were non-cytotoxic to human immortalized keratinocytes (HaCaT) cells (>95% viability). At 5-45 μg/mL, they dose-dependently attenuated UVB-induced damage, raising cell viability from 68.54% (UVB control) to 92.45%. CAT exhibited cell selectivity against melanoma cell lines, displaying potent inhibition against A375 cells but weaker activity against B16F10 cells than arbutin. Molecular docking revealed quercetin had the strongest binding to interleukin-6 (IL-6), tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and tyrosinase (TYR). These findings demonstrate that total flavonoids from C. aethusifolia mitigate UVB-induced skin damage and inhibit melanogenesis, supporting their potential for treating UV-related dermatoses.

papers.title: S-propargyl-L-cysteine attenuates ketamine induced schizophrenia-like behaviors and neuroinflammation in mice via inhibition of NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome-mediated pyroptosis.
papers.authors: Wang H, Huang Y, Hu Q, Zhang F, Wang Z, Zeng J et al.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) is a serious neuropsychiatric disorder with a complex etiology. Neuroinflammation has received much attention as a crucial contributor to the pathogenesis of SCZ. S-propargyl-L-cysteine (SPRC), a synthesized analog of S-allyl-L-cysteine, increases endogenous hydrogen sulfide (H2S) synthesis and exerts potent antioxidative and anti-inflammatory effects. However, its potential role in SCZ-related neuroinflammation remains unclear. The aim of the present study was to investigate whether SPRC protects against ketamine-induced schizophrenia-like symptoms and to explore underlying mechanisms related to cystathionine-γ-lyase (CSE)/H2S signaling and nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) activation. Behavioral alterations were assessed using the open-field test, Y-maze test, and prepulse inhibition analysis. Neuronal damage in the hippocampus was evaluated using Nissl staining, while changes in the CSE/H2S pathway, mature brain-derived neurotrophic factor (mBDNF), inflammatory pathways, and pyroptosis pathway were also analyzed. SPRC was found to effectively reverse ketamine-induced hyperactivity and anxiety, as well as improve working memory and sensorimotor gating defects. Furthermore, SPRC prevented neuronal loss across the hippocampal CA1, CA3, and dentate gyrus subregions. The mechanism of action involves the reversal of CSE activity and H2S production, maintenance of mBDNF, as well as the suppression of NF-κB translocation. This is also characterized by reduction in tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) and interleukin-6 (IL-6) production. Additionally, SPRC inhibited nucleotide-binding oligomerization domain-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, caspase-1-mediated pyroptosis, and interleukin-1β (IL-1β) secretion. Taken together, these findings demonstrate that SPRC alleviates ketamine-induced behavioral deficits and neuroinflammation in mice, likely via restoration of the CSE/ H2S pathway and suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3-mediated pyroptosis.

papers.title: Chemical Characterization and Mechanism Analysis of Ganjianglingzhu Decoction in the Treatment of Low Back Pain Based on UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS and Network Pharmacology.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.authors: Chen B, Li P, Shi J, Xu F, Sun S
papers.abstract:
Ganjianglingzhu decoction (GJLZD), a classical traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formula, has been widely used in the treatment of low back pain. However, its chemical composition and underlying mechanisms remain insufficiently elucidated.
The chemical profile of GJLZD was comprehensively characterized by UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS. Representative bioactive constituents were subsequently selected for target prediction using the PharmMapper and SwissTargetPrediction databases. Overlapping targets between compound-related targets and low back pain-related targets retrieved from the GeneCards database were subjected to protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis, Gene Ontology (GO), and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses, as well as molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation.
Based on MS/MS fragmentation patterns and literature comparison, a total of 58 constituents were tentatively characterized from GJLZD. These mainly included flavonoids, alkaloids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids. We identified 466 overlapping targets between the active components and low back pain. PPI analysis highlighted SRC, PIK3CA, and AKT1 as the major hub targets. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses suggested that these targets were primarily involved in signal transduction, inflammatory regulation, and metabolism. The enriched pathways included VEGF, FcεRI, and AGE-RAGE signaling. Molecular docking revealed that neoglycyrol showed the strongest binding affinity to AKT1, with a binding energy of -7.93 kcal/mol. MD simulation further confirmed the stability of the neoglycyrol-AKT1 complex over 100 ns.
This study systematically characterized the chemical constituents of GJLZD and elucidated its potential mechanisms in treating low back pain. The results suggest a multicomponent and multi-target mode of action. The integrated strategy combining UPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS with network pharmacology and molecular simulations proved valuable for investigating the pharmacological basis of TCM formulas. Further experimental validation is still needed to confirm these findings.

summary.limitations: 예측 기반 분석 연구로, 실제 치료 효과와 안전성은 직접 검증되지 않았다.

papers.title: Authentication of the Botanical Origins of Curcumae Radix Based on DNA Barcoding and HS-GC-IMS.
papers.journal: Rapid communications in mass spectrometry : RCM
papers.authors: Jiang Q, Yin J, Han X, Yong J, Sun R, Liu M et al.
papers.abstract:
As a classic multiorigin herbal medicine, the precise authentication of Curcumae Radix (Yujin) is crucial for ensuring market standardization and clinical efficacy. Given the complexity of herbal materials, single-method identification often lacks the resolution required to distinguish between closely related species or handle degraded with significant DNA degradation.
A two-dimensional analytical strategy was applied to 24 batches of Curcumae Radix samples. This approach combined ITS2 DNA barcoding for genetic identification with headspace gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (HS-GC-IMS) to analyze volatile organic compound (VOC) profiles. The resulting HS-GC-IMS data were processed using chemometric tools, including principal component analysis (PCA) and partial least squares-discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), to compare and differentiate the decoction pieces.
The results demonstrated that while ITS2 DNA barcoding effectively identified Curcuma kwangsiensis S. G. Lee et C. F. Liang, it failed to discriminate between the closely related species Curcuma longa L. and Curcuma phaeocaulis Val. and was ineffective for DNA-degraded samples of Curcuma wenyujin Y. H. Chen et C. Ling. Conversely, HS-GC-IMS successfully established distinct VOC fingerprints for each source. When coupled with chemometric analysis, this method pinpointed specific interspecific discriminatory biomarkers that allowed for clear differentiation where genetic barcoding fell short.
By integrating stable genetic information with volatile chemical fingerprints, this study establishes a complementary two-dimensional identification system. This strategy provides an innovative and reliable solution for the botanical authentication and quality control of Curcumae Radix, offering a broadly applicable paradigm for the precise identification of other complex herbal materials.
papers.title_ko: DNA 바코딩과 HS-GC-IMS 기반의 Curcumae Radix 식물 기원 감정

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Liu L, Guo Z, Jiang S, Yang M, Zhang Y, Hu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
The prevalence of chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is relatively high and increases with age. The use of sedatives, along with the incidence of their adverse effects, is also rising, which can easily lead to health risks and negative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of acupuncture-assisted zolpidem tartrate tapering and discontinuation in patients with CID whose insomnia symptoms are clinically stable while taking zolpidem.
This study is designed as a single-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial.Ninety participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the acupuncture group or the sham acupuncture group. Each participant will undergo 24 sessions of either acupuncture or sham acupuncture, in conjunction with zolpidem tartrate tapering therapy, over a duration of 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up observation period. The primary outcome is the discontinuation rate of zolpidem tartrate at week 8. Secondary outcomes include the reduction rate of zolpidem tartrate, the discontinuation rates at weeks 10 and 12, frequency of zolpidem tartrate use (nights/week), average daily dose (mg/day), total weekly dose (mg/week), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder -7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Short Form Health Survey-12 (SF-12), sleep diary-related indicators, Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep Scale -16 (DBAS-16), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and emergency medication usage. Adverse events will also be monitored throughout the study. Efficacy analyses will be conducted on the intention-to-treat population.
The findings of the study may provide preliminary evidence for standardized protocols for reducing and ceasing zolpidem tartrate use through acupuncture assistance. Additionally, this research may offer useful references for patients with CID seeking to safely and effectively reduce or discontinue zolpidem tartrate. These findings may inform future clinical research and larger multicenter confirmatory studies.

papers.title: An integrated UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS strategy for comprehensive characterization of chemical constituents and in vivo metabolic profile of Bupi Yichang pills.
papers.journal: Journal of chromatography. B, Analytical technologies in the biomedical and life sciences
papers.authors: Han Y, Li H, Chen C, Xie Y, Xu K, Zhu F et al.
papers.abstract: Bupi Yichang Pills (BYP) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) prescription used for spleen-deficiency diarrhea and chronic colitis, yet its pharmacodynamic material basis remains unclear. This study employed UHPLC-Q-TOF-MS/MS to comprehensively characterize the chemical constituents of BYP in vitro and to identify prototype compounds and metabolites in rat plasma, urine, bile, feces, and tissues. In total, 183 compounds were identified in vitro, predominantly flavonoids, triterpenoid saponins, monoterpene glycosides, chromones, and coumarins. Based on this library, 93 prototype compounds and 98 metabolites were detected in vivo. Tissue distribution showed the largest numbers of compounds in the colon, ileum, and spleen. Flavonoids and monoterpene glycosides were the most frequently detected classes. Calycosin, paeoniflorin, and their metabolites were detected in the brain. These results indicate that the identified chemical classes are the major components detected in vivo in BYP and may serve as the candidate material basis for its efficacy, providing a scientific foundation for quality control marker selection, mechanism studies, and clinical application.

papers.title: Preserved tendon reflexes in a clinically suspected sensory-predominant GBS-spectrum disorder: a case report.
papers.authors: Min X, Liu W, Wang R, Yang X, Ke T, Zhang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Guillain-Barré syndrome usually comes to clinical attention because of progressive weakness and reduced or absent tendon reflexes. Some patients, however, present mainly with sensory symptoms and still have preserved reflexes, making early diagnosis more difficult.
A 71-year-old Han Chinese man presented with distal paresthesia after an episode of diarrhea, and the symptoms became noticeably worse over the next 2 days. The sensory disturbance spread in a glove-and-sock pattern and was accompanied by heaviness in the legs, difficulty walking, and mild distal weakness. Neurological examination showed reduced distal superficial sensation, preserved tendon reflexes, and no pathological reflexes. Brain MRI showed no clinically relevant abnormality, and spinal MRI showed degenerative changes without a definite central lesion explaining the symptoms. Cerebrospinal fluid showed protein of 590 mg/L with a reported white blood cell count of 0.001 × 106/L, a pattern compatible with albuminocytologic dissociation. Because nerve conduction studies and electromyography were not completed during hospitalization, the diagnosis remained a clinically suspected sensory-predominant disorder within the GBS spectrum rather than electrophysiologically confirmed classic GBS. Clinical notes recorded improvement during hospitalization, and the patient regained independent ambulation after receiving intravenous immunoglobulin alongside supportive and adjunctive therapies. At a telephone follow-up approximately 12 months later, he reported no recurrence; no objective follow-up examination was available.
In patients with acute symmetric distal sensory symptoms after a gastrointestinal illness, preserved tendon reflexes do not by themselves exclude a GBS-spectrum disorder. In this patient, the clinical course and cerebrospinal fluid findings supported consideration of that diagnosis, but the absence of electrophysiological testing precluded confirmation. This case emphasizes the diagnostic challenge posed by atypical sensory-predominant presentations and also highlights that, without electrophysiological confirmation, both subtype assignment and overall diagnostic certainty remain constrained.

papers.title: Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. stem extract attenuates cigarette smoke-induced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in mice by modulating PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling.
papers.authors: Yang N, Zhai J, Gong J, Zhang Y, Yu L, Wang C et al.
papers.abstract:
Celastrus orbiculatus Thunb. (COT) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its root, stem, and leaf being used for medicinal purposes. COT characterized by the efficacy of dispelling wind-dampness, invigorating blood, and relieving pain, traditional records in Quanzhou Bencao document the use for asthma, indicating that its traditional treatment in lung system disorders. Previous pharmacological studies have demonstrated that the COT stem (COTS) exhibits anti-inflammatory and protective effects in experimental models related to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, the systemically efficacy and molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-COPD effects of COTS remain poorly understood.
The purpose of this study is to systematically investigate the therapeutic efficacy of the extract of COTS (ECOTS) against COPD in mice through metabolomics and serum pharmacochemistry combined with network pharmacology, thereby providing experimental evidence for elucidating the underlying mechanisms through which ECOTS exerts its therapeutic effects on COPD.
Cigarette smoke (CS)-induced COPD-like mouse model was established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of ECOTS. The potential biomarkers were identified by metabolomics. The blood-entering components were profiled by serum pharmacochemistry. The primary targets and signaling pathways of ECOTS were predicted through network pharmacology analysis. These predictions were further validated using immunohistochemical, immunofluorescence, and Western blot.
ECOTS significantly suppressed inflammation and mitigated lung tissue damage in CS-induced mice. Network pharmacology screening and verification experiments revealed that the protective effects of ECOTS may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling in vivo and in vitro. Furthermore, the PI3K agonist 740 Y-P apparently impaired the effects of ECOTS in CS extract (CSE)-exposed BEAS-2B cells.
ECOTS attenuates CS-induced COPD-like pathological changes in mice, and these protective effects may be associated with modulation of the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway and NLRP3-associated inflammatory signaling. This study extends previous evidence for the anti-COPD activity of the COTS and provides a potential mechanistic and pharmacological basis for its further investigation in COPD.

papers.title: Development of a Case Report Form and Practice-Based Research Network Pilot Registry for Health-Promoting Herbal Medicine in Korean Medicine Clinics.
papers.authors: Jang S, Cheon C, Jegal KH, Yang C, Kim S
papers.abstract:
Herbal medicine (HM) for health promotion is a growing practice in Korean medicine (KM) outpatient settings, yet standardized outcome measurement frameworks tailored to this context remain lacking. This study aimed to develop a standardized case report form (CRF) for health-promoting HM and to describe the clinical effectiveness of individualized HM prescriptions across key health domains in patients seeking health promotion care within a practice-based research network (PBRN).
The CRF was developed through a four-phase process: domain selection, expert and clinician review, pilot feasibility testing, and iterative refinement, yielding a two-tier instrument incorporating five validated patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs). The CRF was then deployed in a prospective, observational, multicenter registry across 13 KM clinics, and pre- and post-treatment outcomes were compared using paired t-tests.
A two-tier CRF with five validated PROMs was finalized and deployed within the PBRN. Of 100 enrolled participants who received HM for health promotion, 39 completed both assessments. Statistically significant improvements were observed in four of five symptom domains - sleep discomfort, psychological stress, digestive discomfort, and urinary discomfort (all p<0.05) - while fatigue showed a non-significant trend toward improvement.
This study demonstrates the feasibility of developing and deploying a standardized CRF within a community-based KM PBRN. Preliminary, hypothesis-generating observations suggest potential symptom-level improvement across multiple functional domains; however, given the small per-protocol sample, absence of a control group, and heterogeneity across sites and concomitant treatments, these findings should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in larger, controlled studies.

papers.title: Association of midbrain IL-6 with impaired nest-building behavior and therapeutic effect of Ninjin'yoeito in old hindlimb-unloading mice.
papers.authors: Matsubara Y, Mizuno K, Yakabe M, Ogawa S
papers.abstract: Psychiatric symptoms can substantially impact rehabilitation outcomes in older patients with disuse syndrome. However, the mechanisms underlying these psychiatric symptoms remain poorly understood, and no established treatment is currently available. This study used hindlimb unloading (HU) as a model of disuse syndrome in old male mice to evaluate the effects of Ninjin'yoeito (NYT), a traditional Japanese herbal medicine. After 2 weeks of HU, old mice underwent the nest building test to evaluate goal-directed behavior, and the open field and elevated plus maze tests to assess anxiety-like behavior. Compared to age-matched sham mice, HU-subjected mice showed declines in nest building and locomotor activity but no appreciable anxiety-like behavior during reloading period. Seven days after HU, IL-6 expression was elevated in the midbrain and was co-expressed with microglia in the ventral tegmental area (VTA). In young mice, intra-VTA injection of IL-6 impaired nest building behavior. In activated primary microglial cultures, NYT reduced IL-6 mRNA expression. During recovery from HU, repeated NYT administration improved nest building and motor function while reducing midbrain IL-6 protein levels in old mice. These findings suggest that elevated IL-6 expression in midbrain/VTA is associated with the impairment of goal-directed behavior after HU and that this impairment can be attenuated by NYT. Collectively, these preclinical findings suggest that pharmacological intervention may provide a therapeutic approach for psychiatric-like behavioral changes associated with disuse syndrome.

summary.question: 비사용 증후군 모델에서 중뇌 IL-6 증가가 목표지향적 행동 저하와 관련되는지, 그리고 닌진요에이토가 이를 완화하는지 평가하였다.
summary.methods: 노령 수컷 마우스의 뒷다리 부유 모델에서 둥지 짓기, 운동활동, 불안 유사 행동을 평가하고, 중뇌 IL-6 발현과 미세아교세포 연관성을 확인했으며, 닌진요에이토 처리 효과를 비교한 전임상 연구이다.
summary.results: 비사용 후 마우스에서 둥지 짓기와 운동기능이 감소했고 중뇌/VTA의 IL-6가 증가했으며, 닌진요에이토는 미세아교세포 IL-6 발현과 중뇌 IL-6 단백질을 낮추면서 둥지 짓기와 운동기능 저하를 완화했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 비사용 증후군과 관련된 정신행동 변화에서 중뇌 염증 신호가 관여할 수 있으며, 닌진요에이토의 가능성은 전임상 단계로 해석해야 한다.

papers.title: Effects of acupuncture on cognitive function and brain activation in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: A randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Gong J, Chong Y, Li M, Ma Q, Wu Q, Sun J et al.
papers.abstract:
Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) may represent an important window for interventions to delay dementia progression. Acupuncture, a central practice of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), has been studied as a non-pharmacological approach for MCI; however, clinical and neurofunctional evidence supporting its efficacy remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the effects of acupuncture on cognitive function and brain activation in older adults with MCI.
In this randomized, assessor-blinded, controlled trial, 60 older adults with MCI were assigned to an experimental group receiving 12 weeks of acupuncture plus health education or a control group receiving health education alone. Cognitive assessments, including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and Shape Trail Test parts A and B (STT-A and STT-B), along with functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) measurements during a verbal fluency task (VFT), were performed at baseline and after 12 weeks. Task-related β-values in seven regions of interest (ROIs), such as the frontal pole area (FPA), temporal cortex (TC), and Broca's area, were analyzed.
Among the 60 randomized participants, 56 (27 in the experimental group, 29 in the control group) completed the trial and were included in the primary analysis. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), controlling for baseline scores, revealed a significantly greater improvement in MoCA scores for the experimental group (adjusted mean difference = 4.66, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.76-5.55, P < 0.001), along with greater reductions in STT-A (-11.83 s, P = 0.007) and STT-B (-40.86 s, P = 0.003). fNIRS analysis indicated significant time-by-group interactions in the FPA, TC, and Broca's area (P < 0.05), with β-values increasing exclusively in the experimental group. Cognitive improvements correlated with β-value changes in TC (r = 0.30, P = 0.029) and Broca's area (r = 0.34, P = 0.011).
Acupuncture may improve cognitive function in older adults with MCI, accompanied by an increase in task-related β-values in the temporal cortex and Broca's area.

papers.title: From Established Care to Precision Menopause Medicine: A Clinical-Actionability Framework for Contemporary Menopause Management.
papers.authors: Iuhas CI, Marinescu MM, Danciu C, Ormindean CM, Ciortea R, Malutan A et al.
papers.abstract: Menopause care now spans established hormone therapy, mechanism-based non-hormonal drugs, behavioural interventions, and emerging microbiome- and biomarker-guided approaches. This state-of-the-art narrative review evaluated which dimensions of personalisation are clinically actionable and which remain hypotheses of precision medicine. A structured PubMed/MEDLINE search (January 2020-July 2026), updated to August 2026 and supplemented by landmark studies, current guidelines, and regulatory sources, was synthesized using a four-tier clinical-actionability framework (A, established; B, evidence-supported off-label; C, emerging; D, experimental). Menopausal hormone therapy remains the most effective treatment for vasomotor symptoms and prevents bone loss during use; the 2025-2026 FDA labelling revisions altered risk communication rather than the underlying evidence, and professional responses diverged. Fezolinetant and elinzanetant provide mechanism-based non-hormonal options, while SSRIs/SNRIs, gabapentin, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), CBT for insomnia, and clinical hypnosis remain evidence-supported. Exercise, yoga, acupuncture, soy, and equol are not guideline-recommended for reducing vasomotor symptom frequency despite benefits in other domains. Gut and genitourinary microbiome findings should not be conflated: pooled evidence identifies no consistent postmenopausal gut signature, whereas vaginal Lactobacillus depletion is more reproducible but does not reliably predict symptom resolution. Evidence-based personalisation therefore remains principally clinical; microbiome sequencing, equol testing, and multi-omic treatment selection require prospective test-guided validation.

papers.title: Peripheral Vascular and Physiological Responses Associated with Electroacupuncture in Chronic Nonspecific Low Back Pain: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Wang X, Liu H, Zhu Q, Zou Q, Wang Y, Gu W
papers.abstract: Objective: This exploratory study aimed to evaluate the effects of electroacupuncture (EA) on pain and functional outcomes in patients with chronic nonspecific low back pain (CNLBP), and to investigate objective peripheral physiological responses associated with clinical improvement. Methods: In this prospective, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial, adults with CNLBP received EA at Shenshu (BL23) and an ipsilateral Ashi acupoint three times weekly for 2 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up. The primary outcome was pain intensity assessed by the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), with responder analysis based on the minimal clinically important difference (MCID; ΔNRS ≥ 2). Secondary outcomes included the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), local microcirculatory perfusion, skin temperature, and muscle tissue properties. Results: Compared with sham EA, EA significantly reduced pain intensity after the first session, after six sessions, and at follow-up (p < 0.003; r = 0.70-0.84). MCID responder rates were significantly higher in the EA group after the first session, six sessions and at follow-up (p < 0.003; RR = 3.75 and 6.00 after six sessions and follow-up, respectively). EA increased local blood flow at BL23 after the first and sixth sessions. Skin temperature showed only a transient within-group increase, without a significant adjusted between-group difference. Similar trends were observed at Ashi acupoint, and increased blood flow was associated with pain improvement. Conclusions: EA improved pain and functional outcomes in patients with CNLBP while inducing measurable peripheral vascular and physiological responses. Increased local blood flow may represent a candidate physiological correlate of EA-related symptom improvement. These findings support the exploration of objective physiological markers in acupuncture research.

papers.title: Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation Combined with General Anesthesia in Minimally Invasive Surgery for Lung Cancer: A Randomized, Patient- and Assessor-Blinded, Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Zhang Y, Yan W, Wei J, Wang J, Wan Y, Liu F et al.
papers.abstract: Background: We aimed to clarify (1) the analgesic efficacy of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation (TEAS) combined with general anesthesia during minimally invasive lung cancer surgery and (2) exploratory neural network correlates of acupuncture-drug combined anesthesia. Methods: Eligible patients receiving general anesthesia for minimally invasive lung cancer surgery were randomly allocated to perioperative TEAS or sham-TEAS in this randomized, patient- and assessor-blinded, sham-controlled trial. Postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) was administered. Outcome measures included postoperative visual analog scale (VAS) pain scores, sufentanil consumption via PCIA, and total/effective PCIA pump presses. Perioperative electroencephalography (EEG) was acquired using a 22-lead recorder, and brainwave power spectra were analyzed using Fourier transform. Repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA) was applied to serial postoperative VAS scores at 6, 24 and 48 h. Independent-samples t-tests compared cumulative sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively. Post hoc simple-effect comparisons were performed as exploratory analyses without multiplicity adjustment. The EEG sub-study was exploratory; false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction was used to control multiple comparisons across electrodes and frequency bands. Results: In total, 109 patients were randomized. A significant group-by-time interaction was detected for postoperative VAS scores (F(1.599,171.124) = 68.287, p < 0.001). Simple-effect analyses revealed lower VAS scores in the TEAS group at postoperative 6 h (mean difference -1.900, 95%CI -2.181 to -1.619, p < 0.001) and 24 h (mean difference -1.391, 95%CI -1.645 to -1.138, p < 0.001), with no between-group difference at 48 h (mean difference -0.066, 95%CI -0.320 to 0.187, p = 0.605). The TEAS group also exhibited reduced PCIA sufentanil consumption at 6, 24 and 48 h postoperatively, alongside fewer total and effective PCIA pump presses. After FDR correction, exploratory EEG analysis identified potential dipole-related power differences in the prefrontal, occipital, parietal (postcentral gyrus), temporal and diencephalic regions, predominantly within beta-band oscillations (14-35 Hz). Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest that TEAS combined with general anesthesia may reduce postoperative pain and analgesic requirement. This potential benefit may arise from TEAS-mediated modulation of pain-related neural networks; however, the observed intraoperative EEG oscillatory differences are exploratory neurophysiological correlates and do not confirm causal mechanisms.

papers.title: Motion style acupuncture treatment for traumatic temporomandibular disorder: A case report.
papers.authors: Kwon MJ, Jang C, Lee Y, Kim D
papers.abstract:
Traumatic temporomandibular joint disorder (TMD) tends to persist longer than nontraumatic TMD, and conventional treatments show limited effectiveness in such cases. Motion style acupuncture treatment (MSAT), which induces active or passive movement after insertion of acupuncture needles at the affected sites, may help alleviate pain and improve mandibular movement. However, its application to traumatic TMD unresponsive to prior treatments has rarely been reported, and no case has objectively demonstrated its effects using radiologic findings.
A patient presented with persistent right temporomandibular joint pain and clicking following a motor vehicle collision, which were unresponsive to previous treatment.
The patient was diagnosed with traumatic TMD secondary to the motor vehicle collision, with clinically suspected disc displacement with reduction and concomitant local myalgia.
The patient underwent 6 sessions of MSAT.
Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), maximal mouth opening, and lateral radiography were performed before and after treatment. Pain during mandibular movement decreased from NRS 8 to 1, and resting pain decreased from NRS 7 to 1. Clicking resolved after the 5th session. Maximal mouth opening increased from 25 mm at baseline to 60 mm after the final session. Lateral radiography demonstrated a change in the distance between the articular eminence and the condylar head from 3.43 to 4.81 mm. The patient also reported reduced subjective discomfort.
The patient demonstrated improvements in both subjective and objective outcomes, suggesting that MSAT may have potential as a treatment option for traumatic TMD. However, as this is a single case report and long-term follow-up was not available to assess the durability of treatment effects or symptom recurrence, further prospective studies are needed to evaluate its efficacy and safety.

papers.title: Constitution-specific Health Norms of the Sub-Health Measurement Scale (SHMS V1.0) and factors associated with suboptimal health in older adults: A nationwide cross-sectional study in China.
papers.authors: Chen R, Li HQ, Xia J, Song HR, Zhang HY, He FY et al.
papers.abstract: The theory of traditional Chinese medicine constitution plays a crucial role in personalized diagnosis, treatment, and health management, and has been widely applied in China's public health services. This study aims to establish constitution-specific health norms for Chinese older adults using the Sub-Health Measurement Scale Version 1.0 (SHMS V1.0) and to explore factors associated with suboptimal health status (SHS) among this population. A multicenter cross-sectional study was conducted across 7 geographic regions in China, with multistage cluster random sampling to recruit participants aged ≥60 years. The Constitution in Chinese Medicine Questionnaire (Elderly Edition) was used to classify participants into 9 traditional Chinese medicine constitution types, and SHMS V1.0 was used to establish mean, percentile, and demarcation norms. Data from 24,812 older adults (56.1% female) were analyzed. Health status was categorized into 5 levels: disease, severe subhealth, moderate subhealth, mild subhealth, and health, based on SHMS V1.0 total scores. Significant differences in health scores were observed across age, sex, and constitution types, with balanced constitution individuals showing the best overall health. Poor sleep quality showed the strongest association with SHS, whereas regular physical activity and higher educational attainment were associated with more favorable health status. Constitution-specific associations were found for dietary preferences, age, and body mass index, and random forest analysis identified sleep quality, regular physical activity, and education as the most important variables associated with SHS. This study provides the first constitution-specific health norms for SHMS V1.0 and enhances understanding of the factors associated with SHS among older adults. The findings may inform individualized health assessment strategies and provide a reference for developing targeted health management approaches to promote healthy aging in diverse populations.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture at Front-Mu acupoint group attenuates stress urinary incontinence in rats by modulating oxidative stress and Nrf2 signaling.
papers.authors: Huang H, Chen B, Hu J, Zhao X, Li Z, Song X et al.
papers.abstract: To investigate whether electroacupuncture (EA) at the Front-Mu acupoint group improves stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in rats through modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway. Sixty-five female SD rats were randomized into sham (n = 10) and SUI model (n = 55) groups. SUI was induced by vaginal dilation and bilateral ovariectomy. Successfully modeled rats were randomly divided into model, DMSO, EA, ATRA (Nrf2 inhibitor), and EA + ATRA groups (n = 10 each). EA was applied at Zhongji (CV3), Guanyuan (CV4), and bilateral Dahe (KI12) once daily for three days. Urodynamic parameters (MBC, ALPP), antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, GSH-Px), oxidative stress markers (8-OHdG, 4-HNE), apoptosis (TUNEL, Bax/Bcl-2, cleaved caspase-3), and Keap1/Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression were assessed. EA significantly increased MBC and ALPP, enhanced SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px activities, and decreased 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) and 4-hydroxynonenal (4-HNE) levels (all P < 0.05). EA also reduced the apoptotic index, Bax/Bcl-2 ratio, and cleaved caspase-3 expression (all P < 0.05). Furthermore, EA upregulated Keap1 and Nrf2 mRNA and protein expression (all P < 0.05). These protective effects were partially abrogated by ATRA co-treatment. EA at the Front-Mu acupoint group alleviates SUI, associated with modulation of the Nrf2-mediated antioxidant pathway, enhancing antioxidant defense and inhibiting apoptosis. These findings provide preliminary mechanistic support for further investigation of electroacupuncture in SUI treatment.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Pilates and TENS acupuncture in treating patients with primary dysmenorrhea: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.authors: Embaby HM, Salman AF, Elnahas EM, Elsharqawy AA, Elsharqawy SA, Elderbashy MS
papers.abstract:
This study aimed to detect the effectiveness of Pilates and Transcutaneous Electric Nerve Stimulation acupuncture (TENS) on Primary Dysmenorrhea (PD) in female medical students.
Fifty-two patients with PD, aged from 18 to 24 years old were allocated randomly to two groups: group A (n = 26) and group B (n = 26). Group (A) performed Pilates exercises for 24 sessions 3 times per week and received TENS acupuncture (30 min per session) for 12 sessions, while group (B) received analgesic drugs in the first 3 days of the menstrual cycle for 2 consecutive menstrual cycles. Assessment of pain performed through the Visual Analogue scale (VAS) while the degree of functional ability through the Verbal Multidimensional Scoring System of dysmenorrhea (VMSS).
Pain levels and functional abilities had improved in both groups, with a highly statistically significant difference in post treatment VAS and VMSS scores (p = 0.001 and p = 0.003, respectively) in favor of group (A).
The combination treatment of Pilates and TENS acupuncture is considered to be a safe and highly effective conservative means of relieving primary dysmenorrhea. The use of these approaches helps to alleviate the pain symptoms and increase the level of functionality.
www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT06808529.

papers.title: Sanmiao San Attenuates D-galactose-induced Chondrocyte Senescence by Regulating the FoxM1-p21 Signaling Pathway.
papers.authors: Ren T, Gao T, Zhou Y, Yuan P, Yuan H, Kang W et al.
papers.abstract:
Sanmiao San (SMS), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, is commonly used to treat Bi syndrome and has been widely applied in the clinical management of knee osteoarthritis (KOA) in China. However, its protective effects against cartilage degeneration and chondrocyte senescence, as well as the underlying molecular mechanisms, remain to be fully elucidated.
To investigate the inhibitory effects of SMS on D-galactose (D-gal)-induced chondrocyte senescence and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms and primary active components of SMS.
D-gal-induced senescence models were established in a human chondrocyte cell line and rat primary chondrocytes. Cellular senescence was assessed by senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-β-gal) staining. Colony formation assays were performed to evaluate the clonogenic capacity of chondrocytes. Proteoglycan secretion was evaluated by toluidine blue staining. γ-H2A.X expression was assessed by immunofluorescence. Cell cycle arrest was analyzed by flow cytometry. Transcriptomic analysis was performed to identify differentially expressed genes. These genes were annotated using the CellAge database to screen for senescence-related genes and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) factors. Key SASP factors were further validated by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured by fluorescence assay. The expression of Forkhead box M1 (FoxM1) and p21 was analyzed by quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR), Western blotting and immunofluorescence. The prototype constituents and metabolites of SMS in rat serum were identified by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS).
SMS-containing serum (SMS-CS) attenuated D-gal-induced chondrocyte senescence by reducing the proportion of SA-β-gal-positive cells, downregulating p21 and γ-H2A.X expression, alleviating cell cycle arrest and promoting colony formation. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that SMS-CS upregulated most genes annotated as downregulated during senescence and downregulated a subset of those annotated as upregulated during senescence in the CellAge database. SMS-CS also modulated most SASP factors, particularly interleukin-6 (IL-6) and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), as further confirmed by ELISA. KEGG and GO enrichment analysis of specific drug targets revealed significant enrichment in cell cycle, mitotic processes and cellular senescence, while comprehensive bioinformatics analysis predicted FoxM1 as a core target. FoxM1 inhibitor intervention showed that SMS-CS significantly counteracted the FoxM1 downregulation-induced increases in SA-β-gal-positive cell percentage, p21 mRNA levels, γ-H2A.X expression, ROS levels and SASP secretion, as well as the FoxM1 downregulation-induced decrease in proteoglycan secretion, thereby attenuating chondrocyte senescence progression. UPLC-MS analysis identified the following major prototype components and metabolites of SMS in rat serum: Ferulic acid, Esculetin, Atractyloside A, Inokosterone, 20,26-Dihydroxyecdysone, trans-Ferulic acid + hydroxy, Obacunone + hydroxy, and Atractylenolide III + hydroxy.
These findings suggest that the FoxM1-p21 axis may be involved in the anti-senescence effects of SMS-CS in chondrocytes and could represent a potential therapeutic target for KOA.

papers.title: Comparative sedative effects of subcutaneous injection at GV20 versus intramuscular opioid administration in dogs: A randomized clinical trial.
papers.authors: Pehar B, Maksimović A
papers.abstract:
To compare sedation after butorphanol or methadone administered intramuscularly (IM) or subcutaneously (SC) at Governing Vessel 20 (GV20) in dogs.
Twenty-four healthy client-owned dogs were randomized to four groups (n = 6) receiving either opioid (0.4 mg kg-1) by IM injection or SC injection at GV20. Sedation was scored every 5 min for 35 min on a 21-point scale by three evaluators. Friedman and Kruskal-Wallis tests assessed changes over time and differences among groups; intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) assessed agreement.
Mean onset of observable sedation was 3.5 ± 2.4 min in the pooled SC groups and 10.5 ± 5.9 min in the pooled IM groups. Scores changed over time in all groups (P < 0.001) and differed among groups at every assessment (P = 0.003-0.044). SC-group scores approached 18/21 at 20-30 min, whereas IM-group scores approached 12/21 at 35 min. ICCs were 0.94-0.99. No serious adverse event required intervention or withdrawal.
SC administration at GV20 was associated with earlier and greater sedation than IM administration. Route- and site-matched studies are needed before attributing the effect specifically to GV20 or recommending routine use.

papers.title: Using AI-generated ultra-widefield-like fundus images to assist colour fundus photography in screening for chronic kidney disease: a multicentre cross-sectional study.
papers.authors: Wu R, Yao H, Wang S, Chen Y, Yu L, Li J et al.
papers.abstract:
To develop a generative artificial intelligence (AI) model that derives ultra-widefield-like (UWF-like) fundus images from conventional colour fundus photographs (CFP) and to assess whether these images improve chronic kidney disease (CKD) screening.
This multicentre cross-sectional diagnostic study included 3776 fundus images from 2056 patients at four centres in China and Japan between 2023 and 2024. The generative model was developed and validated using 1865 images from 1049 patients. CKD screening models were developed using 1750 UWF images and their corresponding UWF-derived CFP-like central crops from 909 patients at Ruijin Hospital with patient-level fivefold cross-validation and externally validated using 161 native CFP images from 98 patients at Jiading Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Performance was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and specificity at fixed sensitivity of 0.80.
In internal validation, AUCs were 0.911 for real UWF images, 0.773 for AI-generated UWF-like images and 0.689 for UWF-derived CFP-like central crops. At fixed sensitivity of 0.80, specificities were 0.879, 0.573 and 0.459, respectively. In external validation, AI-generated UWF-like images outperformed native CFP images, with an AUC of 0.707 versus 0.609 and specificity of 0.458 versus 0.344. Retinal vascular features from AI-generated UWF-like images remained associated with renal function indicators.
AI-generated UWF-like images improved CKD screening performance compared with CFP alone. This approach may extend retinal imaging-based CKD screening where UWF imaging is unavailable, but prospective real-world validation is needed before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Deciphering the Material Basis of an Herbal Formula via Integrated Two-dimensional Chromatography, In Silico Screening, and Comparative Pharmacokinetics: A Case Study of Kaiyu Jiangzhuo Formula.
papers.authors: Hou N, Xia Q, Li Z, Cao X, Tian Z, Zhou Y et al.
papers.abstract: Kaiyu Jiangzhuo (KYJZ) is a Chinese medicine formula composed of nine herbs. Its efficacy in alleviating glycolipid metabolic disorders and reducing the incidence of diabetes mellitus in overweight patients with prediabetes has been widely validated. Although our previous studies separately characterized the chemical constituents of the KYJZ decoction and the components detected in plasma, the relationship between chemical profiling and systemic exposure remains undefined. In particular, it is unclear which decoction constituents are absorbed into systemic circulation and how obesity modulates their pharmacokinetic profiles. This study aimed to comprehensively profile the components of KYJZ and identify potential bioactive constituents by integrating in silico screening, comparative pharmacokinetic, and tissue distribution studies. Two-dimensional liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (2D-LC-MS) and a hybrid method (data-dependent acquisition/high-resolution multiple reaction monitoring) were employed to decipher the chemical profile and circulating components of KYJZ, respectively. Components exhibiting high binding affinity for antiobesity targets (composite Z-score >0.4) were selected for further pharmacokinetic study. In summary, 316 compounds were identified in KYJZ using 2D-LC-MS/MS. Among these, 99 compounds were recognized as circulating constituents, and 16 with a composite Z-score >0.4 were specifically selected for comparative pharmacokinetic evaluation in mice fed a normal-chow diet (NCD) or a high-fat diet (HFD). Comparative pharmacokinetics revealed that long-term HFD feeding significantly changed the pharmacokinetic behavior of circulating components in mice, especially protoberberine-type alkaloids. Despite their low plasma exposure, they were detected at their highest concentrations in the liver relative to all other tissues examined, suggesting that the liver may represent a relevant organ contributing to the antiobesity effects of KYJZ. Our findings highlight the capability of two-dimensional chromatography to characterize complex herbal medicines and establish a novel analysis pipeline integrating chemical profiling, in silico screening, and comparative pharmacokinetic analysis for identifying bioactive components in traditional Chinese medicine formulas.

papers.title: In silico analysis of BDNF (brain-derived neurotrophic factor) with active components from Coronopus didymus and Parthenium hysterophorus for potential treatment of obesity.
papers.authors: Nadeem A, Raimi MZKA, Ullah S, Hamadou M, Nandwa J, Shabbir A et al.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a multifactorial disorder that results from complex interactions among environmental, behavioral, psychological, and genetic determinants. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) plays a key role in appetite regulation, energy homeostasis, and body-weight control. Alterations in BDNF signaling have been implicated in obesity susceptibility. Coronopus didymus and Parthenium hysterophorus are used in traditional medicine for the treatment of inflammatory conditions, hyperlipidemia, and cancer. However, the molecular basis of their putative metabolic effects remains not sufficiently defined. In this study, structure-based molecular docking (AutoDock Vina v1. Loos (2025) 2. Siddiqui et al. (2023) 7) was used to assess the binding of (Kumar et al., 2022 26) phytoconstituents from these species to mouse and quail BDNF. Laurifolin (flavonoid), oleanolic acid, and terpenoid R5 exhibited the most favorable predicted binding affinities, with docking scores of -(Siddiqui et al., 2023 7).8 and -(Siddiqui et al., 2023 7).5 kcal/mol (laurifolin), -8.0 and -(Siddiqui et al., 2023 7).6 kcal/mol (oleanolic acid), and - 9.1 and - 8. Siddiqui et al. (2023) 7 kcal/mol (terpenoid R5) for mouse and quail BDNF, respectively. Subsequent molecular dynamics simulations (Schrödinger Release 2019-4) supported the stability of ligand-protein complexes and indicated dynamic flexibility during simulation; notably, laurifolin and terpenoid R5 displayed the most stable interaction profiles with mouse and quail BDNF, respectively. Collectively, these results report three phytochemicals as candidate BDNF-binding compounds and suggest their potential implications for the treatment of obesity.

papers.title: Best Evidence Summary for Preoperative Pain Management in Elderly Patients with Hip Fracture.
papers.authors: Tu Z, Ouyang Y, Zhang Y, Qi S, Yang F, Zhu W
papers.abstract:
Preoperative pain represents a major symptom among elderly patients with hip fracture; however, evidence-based guidance specifically addressing the preoperative phase has not been well synthesized. We aimed to systematically identify, evaluate, and synthesize the best available evidence for preoperative pain management in this patient population.
Following the JBI evidence-summary methodology and PRISMA 2020 reporting principles, a systematic literature search was performed across the databases PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, CNKI, SinoMed (CBM), and Wanfang Data, as well as the guideline websites of NICE, AAOS, APTA, ESTES, ANZHFR, COA, JOA, KHS, UpToDate, and BMJ Best Practice, covering the period from database inception to 29 September 2026. Two reviewers independently conducted literature screening and assessed methodological quality utilizing the AGREE II instrument, the AMSTAR 2 checklist, and JBI appraisal tools. The identified evidence was subsequently graded according to the JBI pre-classification system (2014).
A total of eighteen documents were included, comprising four evidence summaries, four guidelines, one expert consensus, eight systematic reviews, and one clinical decision support resource. The evidence was organized into seven thematic categories: team training, assessment, intervention principles, pharmacological interventions, non-pharmacological interventions, selected complementary approaches, and health education, resulting in 30 best-evidence items.
This evidence summary provides 30 best-evidence items for preoperative pain management in elderly patients with hip fracture. The evidence supports cognitive-specific pain assessment, timely multimodal analgesia, regional analgesia where feasible, and selected non-pharmacological approaches. Recommendations for regional analgesia and for selected complementary approaches apply only where trained personnel, monitoring capacity, and local expertise are available.

papers.title: Antitumor potentials of matrine; molecular and cellular mechanisms and interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.authors: Charoghdoozi K, Dehnavi S, Sadeghi M, Bazrafshani S, Mohammadi M
papers.abstract:
Cancer continues to be the second leading cause of death globally and poses a significant public health issue. There is growing research and clinical interest in natural compounds that possess strong anticancer properties. Matrine, a quinolizidine alkaloid sourced from the traditional Chinese herbal remedy Sophora flavescens, shows a wide array of pharmacological actions, including antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic effects.
This summary outlines the antitumor mechanisms of matrine, focusing on its interactions with immune cells in the tumor microenvironment. It also covers matrine's chemical properties, challenges in clinical translation, and future research directions.
This study conducted a narrative review using searches across the PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases. The primary keywords included matrine, its structural class, and its antitumor and immunomodulatory mechanisms. The literature reviewed spanned from 2001 to 2026.
Matrine has shown a range of drug-related effects., encompassing properties such as antitumor, anti-inflammatory, antiviral, antiarrhythmic, and hepatoprotective, antibacterial, and analgesic properties. Recent research has indicated that matrine exhibits potential anti-cancer properties via various molecular mechanisms, including the capacity to suppress the growth of cancer cells, trigger cell cycle arrest, stimulate the death of cancer cells, hinder angiogenesis, prevention of cancer invasion and metastasis, overcome multidrug resistance, lessen or prevent the harmful effects linked to chemotherapy or radiotherapy when used in combination with different chemotherapeutic drugs, and also exert anticancer effects through its interaction with immune cells. Structure-activity data point to the D-ring lactam as a key determinant of bioactivity, while nanoparticle-based delivery and combination regimens appear promising for addressing matrine's pharmacokinetic limitations. Clinical evidence, however, remains limited.
Matrine is a multi-target natural compound and may have direct antitumor and immunomodulatory capabilities. Existing preclinical studies have identified that matrine is a promising candidate for cancer therapy development. Independent validation of mechanisms, chemical optimization, and specific delivery technology, along with human pharmacokinetic and safety studies, are all key to applying matrine for clinical treatment.

papers.title: Beyond sleep macrostructure: a high-definition review of acupuncture's electrophysiological signatures in modulating sleep microarchitecture (spectral power, spindles, and slow oscillations).
papers.authors: Fu F, Huang Y
papers.abstract: Sleep science has shifted from coarse stage-based metrics toward a microstructural perspective that treats electroencephalographic biomarkers, spectral power, sleep spindles, and slow oscillations as candidate windows onto restorative brain function. This high-definition review evaluates whether acupuncture has been shown to modify these features. Direct evidence from natural overnight sleep is currently very limited: most available electrophysiological studies were conducted during quiet wakefulness, in resting daytime EEG recordings from clinical groups, or under propofol anesthesia. These studies demonstrate that acupuncture or related electrical acupoint stimulation can produce state-, region-, and frequency-dependent changes in EEG power and network organization, but they do not yet establish increased NREM spindle density, improved slow-oscillation-spindle coupling, enhanced slow-wave morphology, memory consolidation, or glymphatic clearance. We therefore distinguish directly observed findings from indirect mechanistic support and from hypotheses that require prospective testing. Plausible pathways include ascending somatosensory influences on thalamocortical excitability, autonomic and hypothalamic effects that may reduce hyperarousal, and peripheral or central neurochemical processes involving adenosine, GABA, serotonin, and BDNF; however, the causal sequence from needling to sleep microarchitecture remains unproven. Future progress requires preregistered, adequately powered, multi-night studies using validated spindle and slow-wave detectors, explicit control estimands, and multimodal measurements. Biomarker-guided and closed-loop acupuncture should presently be regarded as a research framework rather than an established treatment strategy.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture inhibits the nuclear factor kappa B signaling pathway and alleviates knee synovial membrane inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis in a rat model of knee osteoarthritis.
papers.journal: Acupuncture in medicine : journal of the British Medical Acupuncture Society
papers.authors: Lu M, Meng DH, Li T, Luan GR, Luo SY, Liu CB et al.
papers.abstract:
Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a degenerative joint disease that is characterized by cartilage degeneration and inflammation. According to reports, electroacupuncture (EA) can delay joint cartilage degeneration and inhibit inflammation, but its specific mechanisms remain unclear. The objective of this study was to examine the mechanisms through which EA potentially improves cartilage degeneration and inhibits inflammation in KOA.
In this study, we used monosodium iodoacetate injections to establish a rat KOA model and then performed EA. Cartilage morphology and chondrocyte apoptosis were assessed by hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining, transmission electron microscopy and scanning electron microscopy. Levels of inflammatory mediators in the synovial membrane were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Expression of apoptotic factors in cartilage was analyzed by reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and Western blotting. Nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway components were evaluated by immunofluorescence. To validate the mechanistic role of NFκB signaling, KOA rats were transfected with a NFκB-overexpressing lentivirus, and the effects of EA on phosphorylated (p)-p65, p-IκBα (inhibitor of NFκB), synovial inflammatory factors and cartilage apoptotic markers were examined.
HE staining, transmission electron microscopy and scanning electron microscopy showed that EA alleviated chondrocyte apoptosis in our rat model of KOA. ELISA results showed that EA significantly inhibited the expression of inflammatory factors (tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-13, and interleukin (IL)-6) and promoted the expression of the anti-inflammatory factor IL-10 in the synovial membrane. RT-qPCR and Western blotting results showed that EA significantly decreased the expression of apoptotic factors, including the B-cell lymphoma (Bcl-2)-associated X protein (Bax)/Bcl-2 ratio, caspase-3, caspase-8 and caspase-9 in cartilage. Immunofluorescence results showed that EA regulated the NFκB inhibitor protein IκBα and inhibited NFκB p65. In addition, after KOA rats were transfected with an overexpressing NFκB lentivirus, p-p65 expression was significantly upregulated, p-IκBα expression was significantly decreased, and the expression of pro-inflammatory factors in the synovial membrane and apoptosis-related factors in cartilage were significantly upregulated. After EA, p-p65 expression was significantly decreased, p-IκBα expression was significantly upregulated, and the expression of pro-inflammatory factors in the synovial membrane and apoptosis-related factors in cartilage decreased.
EA decreased synovial inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis, thereby alleviating cartilage degeneration in a rat model of KOA. EA reversed NFκB signaling pathway activation after NFκB lentivirus transfection, showing that inhibition of synovial inflammation and chondrocyte apoptosis and alleviation of cartilage degeneration by EA are associated with inhibition of NFκB signaling pathway activation.
